headline: India's rooftop solar boom: 6.6 GW added in first half of year
meta_description: India installed 6.6 GW of rooftop solar in H1, more than doubling the 2.8 GW from the same period last year.
summary_short: India's rooftop solar capacity surged 136% in the first half of the year, with 6.6 GW installed compared to 2.8 GW a year prior.
body:
India installed 6.6 gigawatts of rooftop solar capacity in the first half of the year—a remarkable 136% increase compared to the 2.8 GW added during the same period in 2025.

The acceleration reflects growing momentum in India's shift toward distributed renewable energy. Rooftop solar represents a particularly promising avenue: it decentralizes power generation, reduces grid strain, and empowers households and businesses to generate their own electricity. The sharp year-over-year jump suggests that either installation infrastructure has scaled rapidly, or demand among property owners has surged—or both.

For a nation balancing energy security with climate commitments, this trajectory offers real progress. Each rooftop installation chips away at carbon-intensive power generation while building energy resilience at the local level.
quick_facts: 6.6 GW of rooftop solar installed in H1 2026
